topic: Apollo 13: the square peg in a round hole
claim: After the Apollo 13 explosion in 1970, engineers fitted square command-module CO2 filters to the lunar module's round openings using plastic bags, cardboard and tape, and all three astronauts came home.

beats.vo: A square filter. A round hole.
April thirteenth, nineteen seventy. Apollo 13 is about two hundred thousand miles from Earth when an oxygen tank explodes.
The three astronauts crowd into the lunar module, Aquarius. It was built for two men for two days. Now it must keep three alive for about four.
After a day and a half, a warning light shows carbon dioxide at dangerous levels. The spare filters are square. The openings are round.
Engineers in Houston devise a fix from plastic bags, cardboard, and tape. A square peg, in a round hole.
On April seventeenth, all three astronauts splash down safely in the Pacific. NASA calls it a successful failure.

sources.text: NASA, 50 Years Ago: Apollo 13 Review Board Report (2020). https://www.nasa.gov/history/50-years-ago-apollo-13-review-board-report/
